scalarImport.dateFinding: LibreOffice oleprops.cxx:565 truncates VT_DATE to integral days from 1899-12-31. Microsoft DateTime.FromOADate documentation defines 1899-12-30 plus the absolute fractional day. Import follows the documented stored representation, including negative fractional dates. FILETIME uses UTC and editing duration preserves 100 ns fractions; sub-millisecond timestamps retain their original bytes alongside the normalized string.
scalarImport.remaining: Property export is now implemented for supported values. Raw unsupported property retention, encrypted ancillary-property support and broader native qualification remain open; see scalarExport.

scalarExport.change: BIFF7, BIFF8 and dual-stream exports emit SummaryInformation and DocumentSummaryInformation with UTF-8 codepages, section-relative offsets, padded values and named custom scalar dictionaries. Supported fields include Unicode text, keywords, integer/double/boolean values, revision strings, UTC FILETIME timestamps and exact elapsed-time ticks. Unsupported values produce loss warnings. Properties remain plaintext beside encrypted workbook streams; encrypted ancillary streams are not implemented.
scalarExport.sourceFindings: LibreOffice comphelper string.cxx:367/396 joins keywords with comma-space and splits on commas; o3tl string_view.hxx:417 trims nonzero controls through U+0020, U+2000..200B and U+2028..2029. NUL and NBSP remain. oleprops.cxx:429 reads nonzero BOOL as true and :436 writes signed 16-bit -1. Import now follows those rules. Named values containing commas or trimmed boundary characters cannot round-trip as one native keyword and are diagnosed.

encryptedAncillarySource.flags: EncryptionInfo.java:57-61 and :276-277: flagDocProps bit 0x08 must be zero for encrypted document properties. POIDocument.java:222-229 requires the encrypted container when that flag is clear; :500-501 names it encryption for spreadsheet documents.
encryptedAncillarySource.layout: CryptoAPIDecryptor.java:180-230 decrypts the first eight bytes with block 0 to get descriptor-array offset/size; it resets block 0 at the descriptor array, then reads count and entries. Each entry is offset:u32, size:u32, block:u16, nameLength:u8, flags:u8, reserved:u32, UTF16LE name and a trailing u16 terminator. CryptoAPIDocumentInputStream.java:47-49 resets the cipher at each declared block, independently of stream position. Payloads are not Workbook-style 1024-byte chunks.
encryptedAncillarySource.writer: CryptoAPIEncryptor.java:125-191 writes payloads under consecutive block IDs, then the descriptor array under block 0 and rewrites the header under block 0. POIDocument.java:288-310 places real properties in the encrypted container, removes plaintext SummaryInformation and writes an empty plaintext DocumentSummaryInformation placeholder.
encryptedAncillarySource.keyDerivation: CryptoAPIDecryptor.java:115-129 hashes the verified base secret plus a little-endian 32-bit block ID, truncates to keyBits/8, and pads a 40-bit key to 16 bytes. Reuse the existing BIFF CryptoAPI derivation with explicit key and plaintext-buffer ownership; do not ask for the password again.
encryptedAncillarySource.productGap: At 401ab98040, flagDocProps=0 was refused before password acquisition and decryptBiffRecords had no CFB stream collection. Container import and explicit CryptoAPI property export now reuse the existing key derivation and host capabilities. Its tested 16+ UTF-16-unit RC4 passwords and all 12 CryptoAPI profiles are refused; these are native limits, not product support restrictions. Other applications, ancillary streams/properties, additional applicable profiles and containing publication remain open. LibreOffice 26.8 opens the plaintext control, three standard-RC4 and two 128-bit CryptoAPI profiles. Immutable source explains other refusals and native XLSX error loss; see biff-libreoffice-interop-proof.json. Unknown ancillary reexport now preserves exact payload bytes with explicit property encryption; native application qualification remains open.

AES-CBC, Blowfish CFB8/CFB64 and LibreOffice Argon2id/AES-GCM imports and explicit encrypted exports are implemented. LibreOffice 26.8 opens qualified AES, CFB64 and modern ASCII/Unicode-password exports. Independent crypto and SDK checks also pass modern empty passwords, which the native loader refuses. Broader algorithm/application/platform qualification and containing publication remain open.

On-file-key encrypted imports match native records. Empty effective passwords are refused; plaintext stays default. All seven compiled SDK profiles and the Shell export reopen in native Gnumeric byte-exact with empty stderr. This is legacy obfuscation with a recoverable key and readable schema, not authenticated password security. Wider profiles, companions and final delivery qualification remain open. Owned decrypted buffers now clear on disposal and cancellation, including concurrent abort/cleanup. Physical block 65535 and the five neighboring retained pxlib vectors pass through the compiled decoder with explicit finite limits; no large fixture retained.

Current compiled SDK and Shell match activated Linux Perl date controls byte-for-byte at frozen time 1709166600 in UTC and America/Los_Angeles, with empty diagnostics and preserved Shell input. Wider date/DST boundaries, lifecycle, installed artifacts and publication remain open.

Current compiled SDK/Shell match 625 PERL_SED rows within the complete 633-row activated Linux cohort byte-for-byte. The cohort excludes 13 malformed UTF-8 outputs; wider grammar, Unicode, diagnostics, lifecycle, installed artifacts and publication remain open.
